question: If AI gets cheaper by choosing what to remember and what to forget, what should it keep?
reflection: Smarter engineering that cuts waste can put capable tools within reach of smaller teams, schools and public bodies.

sources.subject: What DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash teaches us about efficient AI

one_line: A deep look at DeepSeek's newest model suggests AI costs now depend more on clever memory design than on raw model size.

top_stories.title: A bigger DeepSeek model that is cheaper to run
top_stories.what: DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash is reportedly almost twice the size of the previous version yet stores about four times less working memory per conversation.
top_stories.why: Lower serving costs make long research and analysis tasks with AI affordable for smaller organisations, not only big tech firms.

top_stories.title: Memory, not size, drives the cost of agents
top_stories.what: The model splits reading and writing into separate stages and lets layers share stored context, so long agent sessions take far less memory to keep and restore.
top_stories.why: Agents that work for hours on documents and interviews become practical only when keeping their context is cheap.

top_stories.title: New questions for choosing a model
top_stories.what: The analysis argues buyers should look at active parameters, memory per word and the cost of pausing a session, not just the headline parameter count.
top_stories.why: Procurement teams in public bodies need simple, fair criteria to compare AI offers on running cost.

idea.title: Plain-language AI cost checklist
idea.pitch: A one-page checklist that helps non-technical managers compare AI services on running cost, memory needs and data handling.
idea.first_step: Turn the four questions from today's analysis into plain wording and test them with two procurement staff.

idea_kids.title: What to keep in the backpack
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom game where children pack a small backpack for a trip and must choose which items to keep and which to leave, then explain why.
idea_kids.first_step: Collect twenty picture cards of everyday items and a paper backpack that fits only eight.

watchlist.name: DeepSeek
watchlist.note: Its memory-saving design may be copied by other open model makers.

terms.definition: The stored working memory a model keeps about earlier words, so it does not reread everything for each new word.
A shortcut where a model looks only at the most relevant earlier parts of a long text instead of all of it.
What it costs to get one complete job done with an AI model, rather than the price per word.

concepts.summary: New model designs cut the memory needed to work with very long inputs.
Strong models get cheaper to run through better design, not only better chips.
